A1.justification: Both complete 18-page PDFs describe the same work. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C are readable and reliably matchable.

before.justification: v1 reports original state-tracking experiments in Section 6 and Table 2, including length-generalization results and an initialization analysis.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments, their numerical results in Table 2, and the initialization analysis.

M1.justification: The DCD recurrence, layer-stacking construction, explicit S3 model, and simplified AUSSM are unchanged. The corrected Mamba parameter domain appears in the mathematical background; no change to the implemented models is reported.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same nine group tasks: C2, C6, C24, C60, C2 × C4, C3 × C6, S3, A4, and A5. No training or evaluation scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same single- and two-layer comparisons among Mamba, Negative Mamba, Simple AUSSM, AUSSM, and RNN.

E3.justification: Section 6 retains training lengths up to 60, testing up to 1000, curriculum learning, and the longest-length metric requiring accuracy above 90%. Model configurations, optimization settings, and search ranges are unchanged.

E4.justification: The simplified-AUSSM comparison and the analysis of initializing AUSSM near the analytical S3 solution are retained unchanged. No ablation, robustness test, or supplementary empirical analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report three random seeds per experiment and select the best result across seeds. Neither adds uncertainty intervals, significance tests, or another statistical reporting procedure.

E6.justification: All Table 2 entries and empirical findings are unchanged. For example, two-layer Negative Mamba still reaches length 360 on C2 × C4, and near-solution initialization still enables extrapolation to at least four times the training length.

T1.justification: Lemma 1 and Appendix C.1 correct the drift condition from |λ_j| = 1 with nonzero b_j to λ_j = 1 with nonzero b_j, distinguishing translation from bounded rotation. Section 2.1 also changes Mamba's Λ domain from nonpositive to strictly negative. These are localized mathematical corrections; the main theorem statements and proof structure remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same expressivity characterization for single- and multilayer diagonal SSMs and the same empirical expressivity–learnability gap.

C2.justification: Section 6 narrows the expectation that Mamba cannot track any group to any non-trivial group, excluding the trivial group from the limitation. The remaining interpretations and applicability qualifications are unchanged.

D1.justification: The FP32 precision, hyperparameter grid, AdamW settings, dimensions, batch size, nonlinearities, residual connections, and initialization details are unchanged. No implementation or code/data-access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography, related-work discussion, and positioning relative to earlier expressivity results are unchanged.

P1.justification: Editing is limited to the mathematical corrections, the addition of 'non-trivial' in Section 6, and updated arXiv version/date text. Section ordering and the narrative structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–5 and Tables 1–4 retain their content, captions, structure, and placement. Visual differences are limited to the first-page arXiv stamp placement and local text reflow around corrections.

improvement.justification: v2 improves mathematical precision by aligning Lemma 1 and its proof with Appendix A's existing distinction between translation and bounded rotation. The strictly negative Mamba parameter domain is consistent with the displayed inverse, and the non-trivial-group qualification removes an overstatement. These useful corrections provide a limited overall improvement; the central claims and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
